quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 16 Questions • Passing Score 12

questions.question: What happens if you shift into a lower gear without going slow enough?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear without going slow enough, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid. This causes you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face and eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what following distance should you keep from another vehicle?

options.text: You do not need to worry about following distance.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane so drivers can see you.

questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least a four-second distance from the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if weather or road conditions are bad.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic, practice on a quiet road first. This lets you get used to how your motorcycle feels with the extra weight.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Glasses or sunglasses are not good enough. In Vermont, you do not need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, like speed limit signs, are rectangular and have white backgrounds with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Keep your eyes focused just ahead of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn just your head, not your whole body. Keep your eyes level.

questions.question: A helmeted rider is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, no matter the speed.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive any vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding, as it will likely stop on its own.
Slowly close the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road. Once off the road, fix what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should have all of these features, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around. Check for no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should:

options.text: Sit either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Not ride on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has a sidecar, your passenger should ride in it. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: You can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: You need more following distance when your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: In a group ride, less experienced riders should be near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They may slow down the group.
They will ride too fast in other positions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: In a group, less experienced riders should ride toward the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them easily.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Use footwear with low heels that won't catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: To lean the motorcycle for a turn, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
